_comment_agent: Plain C enum (NONE=0, DOLBY, DPLII, DPLIIX, DPLIIZ, DOLBYEX, DOLBYHEADPHONE=6, NB=7 count sentinel), no fields, no lifecycle. Every enumerator is non-negative, so the C compiler and bindgen give it an unsigned underlying type (ffi::AVMatrixEncoding is a c_uint newtype); a negative int written into its storage reads back as a large unsigned value, never as a negative one. Stored as a raw int: the payload of AV_FRAME_DATA_MATRIXENCODING frame side data (decoders write the enum into the side-data bytes), SwrContext's AV_OPT_TYPE_INT option matrix_encoding (default AV_MATRIX_ENCODING_NONE, range NONE..NB-1, named consts none/dolby/dplii), and taken by value by swr_build_matrix2. Readers of side data and option memory may see any value, so the Rust representation is a #[repr(transparent)] newtype MatrixEncoding over ffi::AVMatrixEncoding with associated constants, infallible raw conversions both ways, index() into 0..COUNT, Default = NONE (the zeroed value and the swr option default), and CPlainElem (every c_uint bit pattern valid). Corrected by the formats wave-0 review: the previous finding called the encoding c_int.
